passage: Guess who's backing the community garden plan for the old Pine Street lot? The Brindle Street Neighbors Association. Same group that spent all last summer trying to ban leaf blowers. I don't need to read the proposal to know where this is headed. Hard no from me.
cue: Same group that spent all last summer trying to ban leaf blowers
explanation: Doug rejects the garden plan because a group he dislikes supports it, and admits he hasn't read the proposal. The plan's merits depend on its details, not on who's cheering for it.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Doug isn't attacking whoever proposed the plan; he taints the plan through a disliked group that happens to back it.

Ravi: Isn't that what the Thursday-night group keeps telling everyone? The crew that got caught sharing quiz answers last term? If they're on board, I'm out. Chapter 9 for me.

explanation: Ravi drops the study advice because a group with a cheating scandal is also passing it around. Who else repeats the tip doesn't change what the professor's review sheet says.

title: Re: Moving to Trellisboard for project tracking
passage: Thanks, Omar. The per-seat price is reasonable and I like that it exports to CSV, which would make reporting easier. My hesitation: Trellisboard is the Ostrander team's favorite tool, and they champion it at every all-hands. Honestly, anything that crowd gets excited about makes me nervous. Could we look at a couple of alternatives first?
cue: anything that crowd gets excited about makes me nervous
explanation: Beatriz weighs real factors like price and CSV export, then counts the tool against itself because a team she distrusts loves it. Their enthusiasm says nothing about how well it would work for her.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Beatriz isn't attacking Omar, who proposed the tool; she judges the tool by the team it's associated with.

title: Good food, but I'm out
passage: Three weeks in: the produce shows up fresh, portions are generous, and the Thai basil chicken is a weeknight hero. Then I learned the founder spoke at the same wellness summit as the guy selling 'detox' foot pads. That told me what kind of company this is, so I've canceled. Two stars for the food.
cue: spoke at the same wellness summit as the guy selling 'detox' foot pads
explanation: Carmen's own experience with the meal kit is positive, but she condemns the company because its founder shared a stage with a dubious seller. Sharing a lineup isn't evidence about this company.

whyNot.fal_ad_hominem: Carmen doesn't point to anything the founder did wrong; she tars the company through someone else at the same event.

passage: The Lantern Phonics program has solid pilot numbers; I've read them. What gives me pause is who has lined up behind it. It's the flagship curriculum at Corvane Academies, the chain fined last year for inflating graduation rates. When an organization like that champions a program, I think parents deserve better, and I can't support it for Fenmoor.
cue: It's the flagship curriculum at Corvane Academies, the chain fined last year for inflating graduation rates
explanation: Trustee Holloway accepts the pilot results, then rejects the program because a discredited school chain uses it. Corvane's misconduct doesn't change how Lantern Phonics performed in the pilot.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: Corvane didn't create the program; the trustee rejects it because of who uses and promotes it now, not because of where it came from.

title: Standing desks show no back-pain benefit in 900-person trial
passage: Researchers at the Wexmoor Institute found office workers with standing desks reported the same back pain after a year as those who sat. Ergonomics blogger Tessa Vane urged readers to ignore the results, noting the study 'is being cheered on by every office-chair company in the country.' The trial was publicly funded.
cue: is being cheered on by every office-chair company in the country
explanation: Tessa dismisses the trial because chair makers are celebrating it. Their applause came after a publicly funded study was finished, so it says nothing about whether the results are sound.

whyNot.fal_genetic_fallacy: The chair companies didn't fund or run the study; Tessa rejects it because of who's cheering now, not because of where it came from.

title: Dana Price deal: why I want an audit first
passage: Dana co-founded her last two companies with Victor Reese, and both were shut down after regulators found misreported revenue. That doesn't make Dana guilty of anything. But we're being asked to invest on her unaudited figures alone, and that history is a real risk signal. An independent audit before we commit is a reasonable price for confidence.
cue: we're being asked to invest on her unaudited figures alone
explanation: Wen treats Dana's repeated partnership with a misreporting co-founder as a reason to verify, not a verdict. Because the deal rests on unaudited numbers, checking them is a fair, proportionate step.

whyNot.fal_guilt_by_association: Wen explicitly doesn't call Dana guilty; the link justifies an audit of the actual figures, which will settle the question.
